newsitem.title: USA: Fla. jury begins deliberating doctor murder case.
newsitem.headline: Fla. jury begins deliberating doctor murder case.

text.p: Jurors began deliberations Thursday in the first-degree murder trial of a Colombia-born doctor accused of killing a terminally ill patient with an overdose of pain medicine.
Deliberations in the trial of Dr. Ernesto Pinzon began at 12:40 p.m. EDT, a few hours after the U.S. Supreme Court ruled states have the right to prohibit doctor-assisted suicide.
Pinzon could face imprisonment for life if convicted of first-degree murder. The jury also could consider lesser charges of second-degree murder or manslaughter.
In closing arguments prosecutor John Aguero told jurors "Nobody but God can figure out when you're going to die. Nobody but God has a right to take you."
Pinzon, 37, was accused of killing 70-year-old Rosario Gurrieri by injecting him with massive doses of morphine followed by potassium chloride, a drug often used in lethal injection executions.

Gurrieri suffered from lung cancer that had spread into his spine and liver and other vital organs. His personal physician had given him about two days to live when Pinzon began to treat him in October at a Highlands County hospital.
Pinzon testified he was only trying to relieve Gurrieri's pain and had not tried to kill him. He contended that the patient died of his illness.
The case hinged on the testimony of a medical examiner, whose expertise was cast in doubt by a former employer. The examiner testified that Gurrieri died of morphine poisoning.
Defence lawyer Bill Fletcher called that "an invalid opinion based on medical ignorance," adding: "Patients are undermedicated because doctors are afraid to treat pain and you can see why."
Gurrieri died surrounded by grieving relatives who had asked Pinzon to ease his suffering by injecting him with enough pain-killers to put him in a coma.

Aguero, the prosecutor, urged jurors to put aside their sympathy for Pinzon and his patient. "If this killing is merciful, it's murder. If this killing is compassionate, it's murder. The only way this death isn't murder is if the drugs didn't shorten or end his life," Aguero said.
